vocabulary._description: The grammar pin gate (script/m14/verify-grammar-pins.ts) reports three counts for this lane -- ids=301 namedUnique=36 anonUnique=104 fields=2 -- and this file uses the same three so the two documents can be compared directly. `ids` is tree-sitter's whole symbol space and mixes three vocabularies; `namedUnique`/`anonUnique` are its two halves by tree-sitter's OWN nodeTypeIsNamed flag, not by a pattern on the name. This spec buckets by ANALYZER REACHABILITY, a different axis and deliberately not the same partition: `internal_silent` holds anonymous tokens (punctuation, the `---`/`...` document markers) and the two grammar-internal wrappers. The two axes are reconciled in `internal_silent.named_vs_anonymous`.
vocabulary.fieldsNote: fieldCount=2 is the entire field surface of this grammar, and the analyzer reads BOTH through childForFieldName (real-yaml-analyzer.ts:204 `childForFieldName("value")`, :506 `childForFieldName("key")`). This is the one structural property that makes the lane pure-AST by construction: the mapping-pair key and value are addressable by field, so no part of the extraction needs to look at a delimiter or at character offsets in the source.
vocabulary.anonymousTypesNote: 102 anonymous / hidden token types the wired 0.7.1 wasm produces, listed as data rather than as classification rows. None can be a symbol: an anonymous node is a token the grammar never names, and the analyzer reads tokens through their parent's fields (`key`/`value` — the grammar's entire field surface, 2 fields) rather than by visiting tokens directly.

measured._description: Every count here was produced by script/m14/tmp/yaml-f8-census.ts over 1,274 files drawn from EIGHT pinned repositories, walking every named AND anonymous child. The probe is committed so the next reader re-runs it and gets these numbers; nothing in this section is carried over from a previous wave. WHOLE-CORPUS CENSUS 2026-10-09 (lane takeover). `bun validation/m14/fixtures/yaml/lane-census.ts <corpus> [maxFiles] [--pools]` walks the WHOLE corpus through the production path (`getParser -> parse -> analyze`, no `projectRoot`, so it matches `firing-check.mjs`) and counts, per relationship type, the EDGES, the FILES, and the CONSTRUCT SITES read from the tree independently of the analyzer. ANSIBLE, 2,076 files (`.yml` + `.yaml`), 2,076 parsed, 0 failures: contains 83,330 edges / 2,042 files; imports 891 / 307; references 93 / 39; uses 22 / 9; extends 8 / 4; overrides 1 / 1; and **calls 0, exports 0, implements 0, instantiates 0**. THE SITE COUNTS ARE THE POINT, because a sample cannot certify absence and this lane has now been burned twice by assuming it could. `calls` = 0 sites in 2,076 files: a `calls` edge requires a `uses:` key at `jobs.<id>.uses` in a file whose SHAPE matches the analyzer's own "GitHub Actions" signature (`jobs` a mapping AND `on` present), and ansible contains no such file — measured two ways (this census, and a direct search for `.github/workflows` and for a job-level `uses:`). `exports` = 0 sites, and its rule is the analyzer's own `schemaPublicationRole`: the parent path is `definitions`/`$defs` and nothing deeper, or `components.<one of the ten OPENAPI_COMPONENT_CONTAINERS>` AND the document declares `openapi`/`swagger` at top level — ansible has no OpenAPI document. `implements` and `instantiates` = 0 sites AND no node type that could express them: the corpus's ENTIRE node-type inventory is 42 distinct types and NONE contains `implement`, `instantiat`, `new_`, `override`, `inherit` or `export`. That is a statement about the LANGUAGE, not about the corpus. The site rules are validated by exactness on the 33 committed fixtures, where every one of them equals the emitted edge count: calls 2/2, extends 5/5, exports 5/5, overrides 3/3, uses 0/0. A NOTE ON THE TWO INSTRUMENTS' POPULATIONS: `firing-check.mjs` admits `.yml` AND `.yaml`, while `script/m14/incoming-gate.ts yaml yaml 0 --repo=ansible` admits `.yaml` only and therefore measured 13 files of this repository's 2,082 (13 `.yaml`, 2,069 `.yml`). Any comparison between the two instruments' yaml numbers has to say which population it is about. POPULATION STATEMENT, so the two instruments can be reconciled later: every census number in this file was produced from the directory `$HOME/fixtures/repositories/ansible`, admitting BOTH `.yml` and `.yaml` under a 1 MB cap. Measured: 2,069 `.yml` + 13 `.yaml` = 2,082 files on disk, of which 2,076 were admitted (6 over the 1 MB cap) and 2,076 parsed, 0 failures. `firing-check.mjs` uses the same two extensions, so its numbers and this census's are about the same population. `script/m14/incoming-gate.ts`, by contrast, admits `.yaml` ONLY, so its `0 --repo=ansible` run is 13 files — 0.6% of this repository. Any yaml figure in this programme must name its extension set as well as its corpus, because on a `.yml`-dominated repository those two populations differ by a factor of 160.

handled_verified._description: Analyzer-referenced node types, each with the count that proves it was reached in real code rather than recognised by name. A type counts as HANDLED when the analyzer names it in a node-type position AND it was observed in the eight-repo corpus. Handled does NOT mean "emits a symbol": the analyzer can handle a construct by consciously emitting nothing for it, and `flow_node` and `block_node` do exactly that (they are grammar wrappers whose only role is to carry an anchor, a tag, or the real value, and the analyzer reads through them). The distinction that matters is handled vs unexamined: nothing in this list is merely unaccounted for. The 8 DIRECTIVE types join the list as of 2026-09-27 (`yaml_version`, `tag_handle`, `tag_prefix`, `directive_name`, `directive_parameter`, `yaml_directive`, `tag_directive`, `reserved_directive`): the analyzer reads %YAML and %TAG directives into `metadata.yamlVersion` / `metadata.reservedDirectives`, resolves a `!handle!name` tag through the %TAG prefix it declares, and reports a reserved directive it does not implement rather than ignoring it. `comment` and `tag` also move here from the gap table, which is kept below as the record of what was open and when it closed. ERROR and MISSING are classified here deliberately: the completeness gate force-appends both to the wasm's named-type list so that a lane cannot leave them unclassified, and the lane DOES handle them — a grammar-error subtree is re-rooted under a `#damaged@<line>` scope with stable per-child identity, pinned by fixture `error-recovery-identity` and mutant `yaml/recovery-scope-renamed`. An ERROR is the grammar reporting that it could not lex; publishing it as a scope is how a configuration language stays navigable when a file is wrong.

resolved_via_parent.alias: alias -> alias_name (the anchor reference; resolved to the anchor's identity, emitted as uses/extends)
resolved_via_parent.alias_name: alias_name is the child of alias and carries the referenced anchor's name
resolved_via_parent.anchor: anchor -> anchor_name (the anchor definition; emitted as a constant under the value it names)
resolved_via_parent.anchor_name: anchor_name is the child of anchor and carries the anchor's name
resolved_via_parent.block_node: block_node -> block_mapping | block_sequence | anchor | tag (a pure wrapper; the analyzer reads through it via valueType)
resolved_via_parent.flow_node: flow_node -> plain_scalar | flow_mapping | flow_sequence | alias | anchor | tag (a pure wrapper; same)
resolved_via_parent.plain_scalar: plain_scalar -> boolean_scalar | integer_scalar | float_scalar | null_scalar | string_scalar (the core schema's dispatch target: which child it holds IS the resolved type)
resolved_via_parent.stream: stream -> document | comment (the file-level container; drives documentCount and comment attribution)

wrapper_handling._description: `block_node` and `flow_node` are the two nodes that make a value addressable without a field, and they are the reason the analyzer can stay field-driven. Neither emits a symbol; both are read through by `valueType` and by `scalarText`.

handled_verified.core_schema_note: `plain_scalar` is a DISPATCH node, not a type. Under the wired build (see design_decision YAML-D6) a plain scalar's resolved type is decided by which of boolean_scalar/integer_scalar/float_scalar/null_scalar/string_scalar the grammar attached. Every one of those five is listed above and every one is observed in the corpus, so the dispatch is evidenced at both ends rather than assumed.

internal_silent._description: Named grammar types the analyzer deliberately does NOT turn into a declaration, each with a reason. This list is NAMED TYPES ONLY, and that is a contract with the completeness inventory rather than a style choice: the gate enumerates the wasm's NAMED node types and reports any row here that the wasm does not produce as GRAMMAR DRIFT. The first draft of this spec also listed 104 anonymous and `_`-prefixed token types here, and the gate correctly reported all 104 as rows the grammar no longer produces — an anonymous token can never appear in a named-type enumeration, so the finding was about the spec's shape, not the grammar. They are recorded as vocabulary in `vocabulary.anonymousTypes` where a count belongs, and no anonymous type is ever a declaration candidate in any case. `escape_sequence` and `timestamp_scalar` live here rather than only in the gap table because the gate classifies a gap row through its `node_type` field and these are defect-style records that carry none — so leaving the types out of every bucket would have reported 11 real node types as unclassified.

named_vs_anonymous._note: All 15 observed anonymous types are structural punctuation: " : - ? [ ] { } , & * ' | > and the --- / ... document markers. The remaining 89 anonymous types are hidden `_rules`, `_repeatN` and `_tokenN` wrappers that never appear as nodes in a concrete tree. Punctuation emits nothing because it IS nothing: in a data language a `:` does not declare a symbol, the pair around it does.

never_observed_named._description: Nine NAMED types the grammar declares that occur ZERO times in 1,274 files across eight independent repositories. Each carries the mechanism that explains it. These are the rows the blind-spot detector exists for: without them they would read as unmeasured holes, and the honest answer for each is different.
never_observed_named.directive_name: 0 occurrences. A child of reserved_directive (`%FOO bar baz`). Reserved directives are removed from the YAML 1.2 spec, so real-world usage is near-zero by design. Mechanism: the construct is deprecated upstream, not unreachable in this build.
never_observed_named.directive_parameter: 0 occurrences. The parameters of a reserved_directive. Same mechanism as directive_name.
never_observed_named.reserved_directive: 0 occurrences. `%FOO bar baz` -- removed from YAML 1.2. Ruled internal_silent with the reason 'deprecated by the specification', not 'unreachable'.
never_observed_named.tag_directive: 0 occurrences across all eight corpora, but REACHABLE and measured: `%TAG !e! tag:example.com,2000:` parses as (document (tag_directive (tag_handle) (tag_prefix)) ...) with tag_handle.text=\"!e!\" and tag_prefix.text=\"tag:example.com,2000:\" (script/m14/tmp/yaml-tag-visibility.ts). Absent from these corpora because %TAG is a schema-authoring tool and none of the eight repos ships YAML schemas. The analyzer handles it (see gap YAML-G3, closed by the directive work).
never_observed_named.tag_handle: 0 occurrences. Child of tag_directive. Reachable, measured, handled -- see tag_directive.
never_observed_named.tag_prefix: 0 occurrences. Child of tag_directive. Reachable, measured, handled -- see tag_directive.
never_observed_named.yaml_directive: 0 occurrences across all eight corpora, but REACHABLE and measured: `%YAML 1.1` parses as (document (yaml_directive (yaml_version)) ...) with yaml_version.text=\"1.1\" (same probe). Absent from these corpora because %YAML is implicit in all of them -- every one is YAML 1.2, which is the default, so nobody writes the directive. Handled (see gap YAML-G3).
never_observed_named.yaml_version: 0 occurrences. Child of yaml_directive. Reachable, measured, handled -- see yaml_directive.
never_observed_named.timestamp_scalar: 0 occurrences, and this one has a NAMED MECHANISM rather than a corpus explanation. The grammar's external scanner selects between three alternative scalar-resolution backends at build time (grammars/tree-sitter-yaml/src/scanner.c:7-11: `#ifndef YAML_SCHEMA` / `#define YAML_SCHEMA core` / `#include _file(YAML_SCHEMA)`), and the wired wasm is the `core` build. src/schema.core.c sets `HAS_TIMESTAMP 0`; src/schema.legacy.c sets `HAS_TIMESTAMP 1` and is the only backend that adds an `RS_TIMESTAMP` resolution result. Measured consequence under the wired build: BOTH `at: 2001-12-14` and `at: 2001-12-14t21:59:43.10-05:00` parse as (flow_node (plain_scalar (string_scalar))) -- not timestamp_scalar. So the type is declared in node-types.json AND present in the wired wasm's 36 named types, and the wired build's scanner never produces it. Ruled internal_silent with the mechanism recorded, and NOT a fixture: writing a fixture for a node this build cannot emit is the provenance theatre #288 was called out for. See design_decision YAML-D6 for the limitation this creates.

gap._description: Every named grammar type is accounted for in exactly one of three places: handled_verified (emitted and measured), internal_silent (deliberately not a declaration, with the reason), or a gap row here. A type that is none of the three is a blind spot. As of 2026-09-27 the two gaps this spec opened are CLOSED (YAML-G1 comments, YAML-G3 tags) and the two that remain are RULED internal_silent with a mechanism (YAML-G2 escape_sequence, YAML-G4 timestamp_scalar), so the open-gap count is 0 — which is a statement about the four rows in this file, not a claim that the lane is complete. LANE TAKEOVER 2026-10-09: the four rows below are unchanged in substance and are refreshed with whole-corpus counts rather than a sample. The open-gap count remains 0 for the four GRAMMAR constructs this file tracks, and the lane's remaining silences are now measured as LANGUAGE absences rather than assumed (see `measured._description`): `implements` and `instantiates` have no construct in the corpus or in the grammar's 42-type inventory.

gaps.why: The analyzer has no comment handling of any kind. A comment is a stream-level sibling of document, carries its own text including the leading '#', and is the documentation surface of a configuration language -- yet 7,938 real comments across all eight corpora produce no docstring, no metadata and no symbol. Matrix 1b lists docstrings as a required payload and the store binds symbol.docstring.
gaps.ruling: CLOSED 2026-09-27 by the analyzer work this gap was opened for, and the spec is updated rather than left claiming an open hole. Comments are now read as document-level stream siblings and attributed POSITIONALLY, not textually: a comment immediately preceding a key at the same or shallower column documents that key, anything else is file-level. Pinned by fixtures `comment-attribution` and `comment-attribution-negative` (the negative twin exists because attribution that fires on every comment is the failure mode, not a fix) and by mutant `yaml/comment-banner-stolen`, which reverts the attribution and is caught. The 'no comment handling of any kind' statement above is the PRE-work census and is kept as the record of what was measured, not as a current claim.

gaps.why: The most frequent unnamed type in the entire lane. An escape_sequence is a token INSIDE a quoted scalar (\\n, \\", \\u00e9), not a construct that declares anything. The analyzer's scalarText reads the parent scalar's text whole, so the escapes are already carried in the emitted value; what is missing is that the analyzer cannot say WHICH escapes a value contains.
gaps.ruling: RULED internal_silent, with the reason stated: an escape is part of its scalar's spelling, and YAML has no declaration attached to one. The alternative -- emitting a symbol per escape -- would be 11,923 phantom declarations in the corpus, which is the fabrication the M14 contract exists to prevent. Recorded as a decision rather than left silent.

gaps.why: The corpus understates this badly and the spec has to say so. 7 occurrences in 1,274 files, and a tag census across all eight repos shows every one of them is a cipher marker (!vault, !unsafe) or a JMESPath fragment, never a type annotation. The construct is far more load-bearing than its corpus count suggests: a YAML tag IS the language's only type annotation, and `!!str 7` is currently classified valueType=integer because the analyzer reads straight through the tag to the scalar underneath. Separately, `!include other.yml` produces zero symbols and zero relationships, which makes a real cross-file import invisible.
gaps.ruling: CLOSED 2026-09-27, and M60 R9 (the declared-type reference graph) now MEASURES the closure rather than merely permitting it. A YAML tag is the language's only declared-type position: the capability was absent until this round — `tag` was in no handled set, so `!!str 7` reported valueType=integer and the tag was read straight through. Four forms are emitted as a closed `declared_type` edge: `!!local`, `!custom`, `!<verbatim>`, and `!handle!name` resolved through a %TAG directive. Pinned by fixtures `tag-declared-type` and `tag-declared-type-negative`, plus `directive-tag-handle` for the directive form. The capability row is measured by script/m60/declared-type-refs-census.ts, which reads `present-declared_type` for yaml (declared=2 typeRefs=2 control=y) after a yaml snippet was added to its table; the lane's reading is recorded in validation/m60/declared-type-register.json. The 7 corpus occurrences still badly understate the construct, as recorded above — that part of the finding was true and remains true.

gaps.why: See internal_silent.never_observed_named.timestamp_scalar -- the wired build is the core schema and never produces this node.
gaps.ruling: RULED internal_silent, mechanism recorded. Carried in design_decision YAML-D6 as a declared limitation because the same mechanism has a user-visible consequence.

design_decision.description: Constructs YAML has no grammar node for, or has no axis for at all. Each is RULED with its reason rather than left as an absence, because 'the language cannot express it' and 'the analyzer forgot it' look identical in an output diff and are not the same finding. YAML-D13..YAML-D16 (2026-10-09 takeover): the project-scoped document identity and why it is safe (D13), the reconciled `calls` silence (D14), the refuted `rpm_key.yaml` external claim and why it is PRE-EXISTING rather than a regression (D15), and the two instruments' differing yaml populations (D16).

decisions.decision: No `calls` relationship. YAML has no call expression: there is no way to write one in the grammar, so the analyzer has nothing to read.
decisions.why: Claiming `calls` for a language with no call expression would be coverage theatre. The M14 spec is explicit that `requiredKinds` must be the kinds a language ACTUALLY emits, not the schema's full list.
decisions.supersededReason: This ruling was written from the grammar alone and the grammar could not see it: GitHub Actions expresses invocation as DATA, so the construct exists in the corpus without existing in the node-type inventory. The corpus census is what overturned it.

decisions.decision: No `implements`, no `overrides`, no `instantiates`. YAML has no object-orientation axis: no class declaration, no method, no member lookup that resolves to a declaration site.
decisions.why: Same reasoning as YAML-D1. Merge keys (`<<: *anchor`) are the one genuine inheritance construct YAML has, and they are emitted as `extends` with the anchor as the target -- which is the closest honest mapping, not a stand-in for a missing feature.
decisions.supersededReason: This ruling was written from the grammar alone and the grammar could not see it: GitHub Actions expresses invocation as DATA, so the construct exists in the corpus without existing in the node-type inventory. The corpus census is what overturned it.

decisions.decision: No `visibility` payload. YAML has no access-level axis: there is no private/package/public in the language, and every key is equally addressable.
decisions.why: An element of configuration is not an access level. Emitting `visibility: public` for every symbol would fill a Matrix 1b cell with a constant that carries no information.

decisions.decision: No `typeParameters`/`genericParameters` payload. YAML has no parameterised types.
decisions.why: The construct a tag fills -- naming a type -- is carried instead by the declared-type reference graph (M60 R9): a `references` edge from the declaration that writes the tag to the type the tag names, marked metadata.relationshipType === "declared_type". That is the honest home for YAML's type information, and it is a graph edge rather than a symbol field because a YAML tag names a type used AT a position, it does not parameterise a declaration.

decisions.decision: `imports`/`exports` are emitted from tag and key SHAPES, not from a grammar construct. YAML has no import keyword.
decisions.why: The constructs that genuinely import another file are `!include`/`!import` tags (Ansible) and a CI step's `uses:` key (GitHub Actions). Both are addressable purely from node type and position -- a tag whose text names a tag-handle plus a path-like scalar, and a mapping pair whose key node's text is `uses`. Measured corpus support is uneven and declared as such: 237 `uses:` sites across gh-cli's 25 files, and ZERO `!include` in any of the eight corpora, so the tag half rests on fixtures.

decisions.decision: The wired grammar is the `core` (YAML 1.2) schema build, and a file that opens `%YAML 1.1` is still resolved with 1.2 scalar rules. Declared as a limitation rather than worked around.
decisions.why: grammars/tree-sitter-yaml/src/scanner.c:7-11 selects the backend at compile time and the published wasm is the `core` one. YAML 1.1 and 1.2 genuinely disagree (`yes`/`no`/`on`/`off` as booleans, octal 0777, sexagesimal 1:30), and no build of this grammar resolves a 1.1 file with 1.1 rules while also being the published artifact. Switching to the `legacy` backend would mean replacing the newest published bytes with a local build whose entire gain is one scalar type, and would make this lane's typing disagree with every YAML 1.2 consumer reading the same file. The decision is therefore to PIN the core build and DECLARE the limitation, and to record the declined alternative with its measurement in the grammar pin's `alternatives` (script/m14/verify-grammar-pins.ts, lane yaml). Changing what is shipped is a separate act with its own A/B under script/m14/verify-grammar-leaves.ts.

decisions.decision: An anonymous scalar sequence item is a VALUE, not a declaration, and does not become a symbol. An object- or array-valued sequence item DOES, as `item_<index>` under the parent path plus `[index]`.
decisions.why: src/ast/parallel-indexer.ts:2390-2394 names YAML merge keys as a legitimate symbol contract that must survive the name filter, and the parallel-indexer comment records that the narrow filter is applied to verified analyzer output precisely for contracts like this. A list of strings is data; a list of objects is a set of records, and the records are what a reader navigates to.

decisions.decision: Duplicate mapping keys in one mapping get disambiguated identities rather than one shared identity.
decisions.why: Duplicate keys are invalid YAML, so this is not a shape to model -- it is a shape to survive. Two symbols sharing one id and one qualifiedName makes every relationship endpoint addressed to that key ambiguous, because the graph resolves relationships by qualified name while the store's own primary key is `${fileId}:${name}:${startLine}` (src/ast/parallel-indexer.ts:2259). The analyzer must therefore keep its identities at least as specific as the store's, or it silently loses an edge.

decisions.subject: calls
decisions.decision: EMITTED, and the previous ruling that YAML has no call expression is withdrawn. YAML has no call EXPRESSION, which is what the old ruling measured, but GitHub Actions expresses invocation as DATA: a `uses:` key directly under `jobs.<job>` names a reusable workflow that the job invokes. The role is decided by the path the analyzer built for the entry, never by the characters of the value, because `acme/infra/x.yml@v3` and `actions/checkout@v4` both contain a `/` and only one of them names a workflow.
decisions.probe: Counted on the parse tree: every mapping pair whose ancestor key chain is exactly `jobs.<jobId>.uses`. The role is the chain, not the value; a value-shape probe would return a different and wrong number.
decisions.measured: 196 occurrences in 92 of the 16371 admitted yaml files, whole corpus, no sampling.
decisions.overturn: Any corpus file with a `uses:` key under `jobs.<job>` whose value does not name a reusable workflow — which would mean the chain is not sufficient evidence and the edge would need a second condition.
decisions.why: The old ruling made the same mistake the workstream document records for the gate first version: it treated the absence of a node type as the absence of the construct. Invocation in a configuration language is a value in a reserved position, and a grammar inventory cannot see it. Confidence is 1.0 because the role is a parse fact — GitHub Actions admits nothing else at `jobs.<id>.uses` — while `resolved` is false because the target workflow is another file and this analyzer is per-file. The edge is withheld, not downgraded, when the document does not claim to be a workflow.

decisions.subject: implements
decisions.decision: RULED — YAML has no construct that expresses interface satisfaction.
decisions.resolution: NOT EMITTED, and the ruling is a GRAMMAR INVENTORY plus a KEY-SPACE probe rather than prose (this `resolution` key is what script/m14/ontology-coverage-gate.ts's `rulingFor` reads; until 2026-10-10 this decision carried only `decision`/`why`, so the arbiter found NO ruling source for implements and REFUSED to report the lane at all). YAML has no construct that expresses interface satisfaction: the wired grammar declares 36 named types (301 node-type ids) and NONE is a declaration of any kind — 0 of `class_declaration` / `interface_declaration` / `declaration` / `type_declaration` / `extends_clause` / `implements_clause` / `base_class_clause` is produced. The key space, which a node-type inventory cannot see, was probed at 18,368 distinct attribute keys over 296,009 sites; the 329 conformance-keyword sites (`implements`/`interface`/`protocol`/`trait`/`impl`/`conforms`/`satisfies`) are counted and excluded as DATA — a keyword key is a site only when the document also declares a type the relation names, and yaml has no type-declaration construct. Attested over node-types + block-types + attribute-keys by validation/m14/fixtures/yaml/ruling-attestation.json against artefact validation/m14/fixtures/yaml/ontology-census.json (0 construct sites).
decisions.probe: Enumerated every node type the wired tree-sitter-yaml grammar produces across all 16371 admitted files: 47 distinct types, against 36 declared in grammars/tree-sitter-yaml/src/node-types.json. None of the 47 is a declaration of any kind; the named nodes are containers (flow_node, block_mapping, block_mapping_pair, block_sequence, flow_sequence), scalars (plain/string/double_quote/single_quote/integer/float/boolean/null/block/timestamp), anchor, alias, tag, document, stream and the punctuation tokens.
decisions.measured: 0 declaration nodes. Two positive probes were run and REJECTED as false positives rather than reported as support: (a) 111 occurrences of `extends:`/`inherits:` keys in 92 files — these are yamllint and Azure-pipeline CONFIG keys meaning "inherit this configuration", not type conformance, and the probe matches the spelling rather than the role; (b) 15 distinct tag texts (55x `!include`, 31x `!unsafe`, 26x `!vault`, 12x `!reset`, 12x `!override`, 2x `!Sub`, 2x `!GetAtt`, 1x `!ENV`, and 6 `!!` core-schema tags) — a tag names the TYPE OF A VALUE and carries no declaration of conformance.
decisions.overturn: A corpus file containing a custom tag that names an interface, or any `!<...>` construct whose semantics is "this value satisfies that type" as distinct from "this value IS that type". The `!!python/object:` family would be such a construct if it appeared: the corpus contains `!!python/name:` (4 occurrences) and `!!ruby/object:RI::ClassDescription` (1), both of which NAME a type, and neither of which constructs an instance of it.
decisions.why: Interface satisfaction needs two declarations and a relation between them. YAML has one construct that binds a name to a value, and `!!python/name:module.attr` names a type without declaring conformance to anything, so there is nothing for an `implements` edge to join. The 111 `extends:` config keys are the trap here and are named explicitly so the next lane does not read them as support.

decisions.subject: instantiates
decisions.decision: RULED — YAML has no construct that expresses construction of a value.
decisions.resolution: NOT EMITTED (`instantiates`), and the ruling is a GRAMMAR INVENTORY plus a KEY-SPACE probe rather than prose (this `resolution` key is what script/m14/ontology-coverage-gate.ts's `rulingFor` reads, and it must spell the type name literally; see the note on YAML-D10). YAML has no construct that expresses construction of a value: 0 of `new_expression` / `object_creation` / `constructor_call` / `class_instance` / `instance` is among the wired grammar's 36 named types, and the inventory contains no construction form of any kind. The key space was probed at 18,368 distinct attribute keys over 296,009 sites; the 14 construction-keyword sites (`new`/`instantiate`/`newinstance`/`create`/`construct`/`clone`) are config DATA (`create: true` in a manifest, `create: x.yml` in a task), not construction. Attested over node-types + block-types + attribute-keys by validation/m14/fixtures/yaml/ruling-attestation.json against artefact validation/m14/fixtures/yaml/ontology-census.json (0 construct sites).
decisions.probe: The same 47-type grammar inventory as YAML-D10, plus the tag inventory: 15 distinct tag texts over the whole corpus, listed in YAML-D10. None constructs an object.
decisions.measured: 0 construction nodes. 0 tags with construction semantics.
decisions.overturn: A corpus file using a tag whose semantics is "build an instance of this class" — `!!python/object:module.Class` is the canonical example and would be a real counterexample, since PyYAML turns it into an instance. It does not occur: the corpus carries `!!python/name:` four times, which names a Python attribute and resolves to the object it denotes rather than constructing one.
decisions.why: A `$ref` into `components.schemas` is a reference to a definition, not a construction of a value, and the analyzer already emits it as `references`. Reading a schema reference as instantiation would put a `instantiates` edge in `bb_graph` that `bb_migrate` would then read as a type to rewrite.

decisions.subject: overrides
decisions.decision: EMITTED, and the `overrides` half of the old YAML-D2 is withdrawn. A duplicate mapping key is a replacement, and the analyzer already gives the two entries distinct identities (`root.child` and `root.child#2`, see YAML-D8), which is what makes an edge between them possible at all.
decisions.probe: Counted on the parse tree: for each mapping pair, compare its key against every EARLIER sibling pair in the SAME mapping. A parent-type test for a pair never fires — a pair's parent is `block_mapping`/`flow_mapping`, never another pair — so an earlier version of this probe counted 0 and the construct looked absent.
decisions.measured: 20 duplicate-key pairs in 17 of the 16371 admitted yaml files, whole corpus.
decisions.overturn: A corpus file where two occurrences of one key sit in DIFFERENT documents of a multi-document stream. Documents are independent namespaces rather than layered ones, so that would not be an override either — which is why the probe is scoped to one mapping.
decisions.why: The two entries are a parse fact. That the later REPLACES the earlier is loader behaviour and not a grammar guarantee: YAML 1.2 leaves duplicate mapping keys undefined, mainstream loaders take the last value, and GitHub Actions rejects such a file outright. The edge therefore carries confidence 0.8 with a reason code and evidenceClass `inferred`, while `resolved` is true because both endpoints are symbols of this file. The chain is last-wins rather than all-to-first, and a mutant pins that distinction.

decisions.subject: document identity / AnalyzeContext.projectRoot
decisions.decision: EMITTED, and TAKEN OVER as unowned work. A document's identity was its filesystem BASENAME, and a basename is not unique in a project: `hostports0.yaml` occurs 156 times in one repository and `Chart.yaml` 243 times, so every member of those documents was a name with 156 declarations and the `contains` edge asserting containment could be walked in NEITHER direction. The identity is now scoped by the file's PROJECT-RELATIVE DIRECTORY CHAIN, dot-joined so no second path convention enters the key space, with the BASENAME LAST so the store's leaf matching is unchanged. It rides on `AnalyzeContext.projectRoot`, ADDITIVE AND OPTIONAL — absent means "this caller does not know which project the file is in", which is every pre-existing caller's behaviour.
decisions.why_it_is_safe_for_other_lanes: MEASURED, not asserted: of the 60-odd analyzers only `real-yaml-analyzer.ts` (committed with this work) and the json lane's own uncommitted copy read `context.projectRoot`; `real-dart-analyzer`'s and `real-typescript-analyzer`'s `projectRoot` are unrelated local fields, and every other analyzer does not mention the name at all. `pool-worker.ts` only ADDS a key to a context object it already returned. So the change cannot alter any other lane's behaviour. The full fixture suite after the takeover reports yaml 33/0, sql 17/0, json 17/0, fsharp 15/0, and its only two regressions are zig and dart, whose analyzers and fixtures are concurrently dirty from their own lanes and which cannot read the field.
decisions.probe: `npx tsx script/m14/incoming-gate.ts yaml yaml 60` reads 1,512 edges, 1,510 resolved, **0 ambiguous, 0 unresolved**, 2 verified external, 0 refuted, control fired — a PASS, and the only lane of 23 that passes. Corpus-scale magnitude of the defect it removes, measured without a project root: ansible 2,076 files, 83,330 `contains` edges of which **17,215 (20.7%) are ambiguous by declaration count**.

decisions.subject: calls
decisions.decision: FIRES ON THE FIXTURES, NOT ON THIS CORPUS, and the reconciliation is a SAMPLING statement rather than a defect. `firing-check.mjs` reported `calls` silent while `yaml/workflow-call-role` pins a `calls` edge; both are correct about their own population. A `calls` edge requires a `uses:` key at `jobs.<id>.uses` in a file whose shape matches the analyzer's "GitHub Actions" signature, and the ansible corpus contains no GitHub workflow at all.
decisions.probe: `bun validation/m14/fixtures/yaml/lane-census.ts $HOME/fixtures/repositories/ansible 0` -> `calls 0 edges, 0 sites in 2,076 files`, where the site counter reproduces the analyzer's own discriminator (job-level path AND workflow shape) rather than guessing. Cross-checked by searching the corpus for `.github/workflows` and for a job-level `uses:` — both empty. On the 33 committed fixtures the same counter reads calls 2 sites / 2 edges.
decisions.fixture_note: The fixture is NOT wrong and was not changed for this: it holds a construct the corpus draw does not, which is exactly what a fixture is for. What WAS wrong was its `meta.isExternal` key, corrected separately.

decisions.subject: imports / external claim refuted
decisions.decision: PRE-EXISTING, MEASURED, AND DELIBERATELY NOT PAPERED OVER. At whole-repository scope the gate refutes exactly ONE external claim: an `imports` edge whose target is `rpm_key.yaml`, marked `isExternal: true`, while the project publishes a document named `rpm_key`. The rule's `targetOwner` splits a target at its LAST dot, so a bare FILENAME reads as `<stem>.<ext>` and the stem is looked up and found — the refutation is the rule correctly applying its own contract to a target shape it was not designed for. The analyzer cannot fix it from where it stands: with no `projectRoot` there are no candidate paths, so the file claim is unavailable; and DROPPING the marker would move the edge from `externalRefuted` to `unresolved`, which the verdict counts as equally bad. The only improvement available is a VERIFIED file claim, which needs the root.
decisions.why_it_is_not_a_regression: The pre-takeover analyzer hardcoded `isExternal: true` at six sites including tag includes (verified in the diff of commit 37a887590's parent), so this edge carried the same false claim before the takeover. The new code strictly improves the case where the root IS known, by turning the marker into a file claim the project can check; in a population that passes no root the behaviour is unchanged.
decisions.probe: `npx tsx script/m14/incoming-gate.ts yaml yaml 0 --repo=ansible` -> `VERDICT: FAIL — 0 ambiguous + 0 unresolved of 656 edges … 1 external claim(s) REFUTED`; the refuted name is listed as `imports  rpm_key.yaml`. The SAME gate at 60-file scope PASSES with 0 refuted, which is the sample-vs-population asymmetry this programme keeps measuring.

decisions.subject: (instrument populations)
decisions.decision: THE TWO INSTRUMENTS DISAGREE ABOUT WHAT "THE YAML CORPUS" IS, and neither is wrong. `firing-check.mjs` admits `.yml` AND `.yaml`; `incoming-gate.ts` admits `.yaml` only. On ansible that is 2,082 files against 13, because the repository is 2,069 `.yml` and 13 `.yaml`.
decisions.probe: `find $HOME/fixtures/repositories/ansible -name '*.yaml' | wc -l` -> 13; `-name '*.yml'` -> 2,069. The gate prints its own population, which is how this was caught: `population: 13 parsed of 13 sampled (corpus has 13 .yaml files across 1 repos; stride sample)`. Any yaml number quoted in this programme must say which population it is about.

zeroEmissionFacts.label: decorates
zeroEmissionFacts.from: validation/m14/measurements/yaml-emission-census-parse-only.json validation/m14/measurements/yaml-grammar-nodes.json — 161 named node types (of 301 ids) in the grammar's own inventory, served build sha256 e752dc21c359; 0 yaml.tag_with_a_call_shaped_argument sites over the whole admitted population (18997 admitted files in 192 repositories); the near miss 167 yaml.tag_with_a_constructor_argument sites
zeroEmissionFacts.statement:
`decorates` is an APPLIED CALLABLE: the contract says the source is the decorated declaration and the target is the decorator's name, and that the decorated symbol does not invoke the decorator — the runtime applies it while the declaration is created. **NOT `references`**: a reference says the decorator's name is mentioned, which is true but says nothing about application. YAML's nearest neighbour of an applied callable is a TAG WITH A CONSTRUCTOR ARGUMENT, and a tag's argument is a NAME — `!include` (suffix `include`), `!!str` (suffix `str`), `!e!thing` (handle `!e!`, suffix `thing`). The csharp lane's dialect decides it, and the fleet accepted it twice: IF THE CONSTRUCTOR ARGUMENT IS A CALL IT IS AN APPLICATION; IF IT IS A PLAIN NAME IT IS A POINTER. A YAML tag is PASSIVE METADATA that marks a value; it applies no callable, and the grammar has no syntax for a call inside a tag (no expression or call node type exists among the grammar's named types). AND THE CONSTRUCT IS NOT LOST: a tag that names a declaration in its own document is a POINTER, and the lane publishes it as the reference it is.

⇒ MEASURED, over the whole admitted population (18997 admitted files in 192 repositories): 0 sites of `yaml.tag_with_a_call_shaped_argument` in 0 files and 0 repositories; the measured near miss is 167 sites of `yaml.tag_with_a_constructor_argument` in 77 files and 9 repositories, and the difference between the two IS the ruling.
zeroEmissionFacts.falsifier: A YAML tag whose CONSTRUCTOR ARGUMENT IS A CALL — a tag whose suffix carries a call's parenthesis. THE CONSTRUCT IS COUNTED: `yaml.tag_with_a_call_shaped_argument`, over the whole admitted population (and `yaml.tag_with_a_constructor_argument` counts the tags that DO carry an argument, so the pointer shape is measured beside it). If that count is NON-ZERO the application shape IS in the language and `decorates` must be implemented instead of ruled.
zeroEmissionFacts.grammarInventory: 161 named node types (of 301 ids) in the grammar's own inventory, served build sha256 e752dc21c359

zeroEmissionFacts.label: renders
zeroEmissionFacts.from: validation/m14/measurements/yaml-emission-census-parse-only.json validation/m14/measurements/yaml-grammar-nodes.json — 161 named node types (of 301 ids) in the grammar's own inventory, served build sha256 e752dc21c359; 0 yaml.template_component_named_in_a_scalar sites over the whole admitted population (18997 admitted files in 192 repositories); the near miss 245 yaml.template_component_named_in_the_file_text sites
zeroEmissionFacts.statement:
`renders` is the name in a RETURNED CONSTRUCTION: the source is the rendering symbol and the target is the rendered component. The fleet's four implementations agree on the shape (a JSX tag, a hiccup vector, a type argument, dart's `build` returning a Widget) — a template expression that NAMES A COMPONENT. Such forms EXIST in the corpus's YAML files (`{{ template "echo-server.fullname" . }}`, `{{ include "echo-server.labels" . | nindent 4 }}`) AND THE YAML GRAMMAR CANNOT LEX THEM: the tree of a Helm chart template has an ERROR node at its ROOT and the interpolation parses as a `flow_mapping` INSIDE that error, not as a scalar. A component-naming interpolation is therefore ANOTHER LANGUAGE'S TEXT INSIDE A YAML FILE, not a YAML construct, and a YAML document has no expression to return a construction from. The second half is the same fact from the other side: the `{{ define }}` DECLARATIONS live in `_helpers.tpl` files, which the admitted extension set does not carry, so no rendered component is declared in the admitted population either. THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THE TWO COUNTERS IS THE MEASUREMENT.

⇒ MEASURED, over the whole admitted population (18997 admitted files in 192 repositories): 0 sites of `yaml.template_component_named_in_a_scalar` in 0 files and 0 repositories; the measured near miss is 245 sites of `yaml.template_component_named_in_the_file_text` in 69 files and 3 repositories, and the difference between the two IS the ruling.
zeroEmissionFacts.falsifier: A template expression that NAMES A COMPONENT and IS A YAML SCALAR — the construct counted by `yaml.template_component_named_in_a_scalar`, measured against the text-level `yaml.template_component_named_in_the_file_text` over the whole admitted population. If the scalar count is NON-ZERO then the interpolation IS a YAML value and `renders` must be implemented instead of ruled.
zeroEmissionFacts.grammarInventory: 161 named node types (of 301 ids) in the grammar's own inventory, served build sha256 e752dc21c359

zeroEmissionFacts.label: mixes_in
zeroEmissionFacts.from: validation/m14/measurements/yaml-emission-census-parse-only.json validation/m14/measurements/yaml-grammar-nodes.json — 161 named node types (of 301 ids) in the grammar's own inventory, served build sha256 e752dc21c359; 0 yaml.merge_list_with_a_separate_base_clause sites over the whole admitted population (18997 admitted files in 192 repositories); the near miss 1 yaml.merge_sequence_with_more_than_one_alias sites
zeroEmissionFacts.statement:
The vocabulary's own reason a mixin is not `extends` is that THERE IS NO SINGLE BASE and the `with` list is not an inheritance clause — so the mixin shape is a LIST OF COMPONENTS ATTACHED SEPARATE FROM THE BASE CLAUSE. IN YAML THE MERGE KEY **IS** THE BASE CLAUSE: `<<: *a` names a, and `<<: [*a, *b]` names several components IN THE SAME POSITION, which YAML's merge semantics order by PRECEDENCE — an order AMONG BASES, not a supertype chain. So a merge list on its own is common (merging configuration fragments is what YAML merging is FOR) and it is NOT a mixin, while the shape that WOULD be one — a merge list beside a separately named base (`extends:` or `allOf:`) — is the counter. YAML has no supertype chain to compose into.

⇒ MEASURED, over the whole admitted population (18997 admitted files in 192 repositories): 0 sites of `yaml.merge_list_with_a_separate_base_clause` in 0 files and 0 repositories; the measured near miss is 1 sites of `yaml.merge_sequence_with_more_than_one_alias` in 1 files and 1 repositories, and the difference between the two IS the ruling.
zeroEmissionFacts.falsifier: A mapping that carries a merge LIST (`<<: [*a, *b]`) and names its base SEPARATELY (`extends:` or `allOf:`) — the construct counted by `yaml.merge_list_with_a_separate_base_clause`, with `yaml.merge_sequence_with_more_than_one_alias` counting the common merge list beside it so the difference between the two shapes is measured. If that count is NON-ZERO then YAML DOES have the mixin shape and `mixes_in` must be implemented instead of ruled.

zeroEmissionFacts.label: part_of
zeroEmissionFacts.from: validation/m14/measurements/yaml-emission-census-parse-only.json validation/m14/measurements/yaml-grammar-nodes.json — 161 named node types (of 301 ids) in the grammar's own inventory, served build sha256 e752dc21c359; 0 yaml.include_family_tag_at_the_document_root sites over the whole admitted population (18997 admitted files in 192 repositories); the near miss 55 yaml.include_family_tag_at_a_key_position sites
zeroEmissionFacts.statement:
`part_of` is the shared-scope relation: a part SHARES the library's single scope, imports nothing, and cannot be resolved as a separate module, and the direction is the directive's own. YAML's only candidate is the include-tag family (`!include` and its spellings), and it fails the contract's own test on a MEASURED ground, not a rhetorical one: IT PUTS THE FRAGMENT AT A KEY, NEVER AT THE INCLUDING DOCUMENT'S TOP LEVEL, so the fragment's content becomes the VALUE at a key position and no scope is shared. The second ground is the same one the fleet already uses: it is a LEADER-DEFINED convention (pyyaml-include's README calls it 'an extending constructor of PyYAML'), not a construct of the format, and the lane already publishes it as `imports` with the marker `yaml_tag_include`, which is an honest label. The Hasura spellings are not even tags — `tables: "!include default/tables/tables.yaml"` is a QUOTED STRING (`double_quote_scalar`), a fact read off the tree.

⇒ MEASURED, over the whole admitted population (18997 admitted files in 192 repositories): 0 sites of `yaml.include_family_tag_at_the_document_root` in 0 files and 0 repositories; the measured near miss is 55 sites of `yaml.include_family_tag_at_a_key_position` in 25 files and 2 repositories, and the difference between the two IS the ruling.
zeroEmissionFacts.falsifier: An include-family tag whose parent is the DOCUMENT (or the stream) rather than a mapping pair — the construct counted by `yaml.include_family_tag_at_the_document_root`, measured against `yaml.include_family_tag_at_a_key_position` over the whole admitted population. If the root-position count is NON-ZERO then an included fragment reaches the including document's top-level scope and `part_of` must be implemented instead of ruled.

denominator.rule: n = the fourteen vocabulary values MINUS the two the grammar does not express (implements, instantiates) MINUS the four zero-emission facts above, which the vocabulary's own contracts rule out and whose falsifiers are counted by the census. Every remaining type is implemented and measured over the whole admitted population.

runEnvironment.mode: parse-only (constructs only; no analyzer, no per-type tallies)
runEnvironment.chunking: 2,000 files per process, in DISJOINT chunks that tile the admitted set — one process per chunk, because a tree-sitter WASM module's memory grows with every parse and never shrinks (the dart lane measured the wall at roughly 7,600 parses), so a single-process walk that LOOKS complete would measure a fraction of the population while printing a whole-population header
runEnvironment.caveat: THE COUNTS THIS DECLARATION CARRIES ARE ONLY AS HEALTHY AS THE BOX THEY WERE TAKEN ON. At declaration time: load average 1.96 2.96 3.83 on 8 CPUs, 6.4 GB available of 15.5 GB, 4.9 GB of swap in use. This machine spent the afternoon of 2026-10-22 in a 20-GB swap, and a closure measured while the box thrashes is a number ABOUT THE BOX. The chunked walk is what makes the counts safe under that: every chunk is its own process and its own parse, so a slow chunk lengthens the run and CANNOT CHANGE A COUNT.

meta.measuredOnAHealthyBoxRule: healthy = load1 < one runnable task per CPU AND swap in use < 1 GB, both read from /proc at declaration time. The counts do not depend on this flag — the walk is chunked, so a slow or thrashing box lengthens the run and cannot change a count — but the runtime it implies does, and a reader comparing two lanes' runtimes needs to know which box each was measured on.

counterReconciliation.rule: The census instrument DECLARES every counter it maintains and emits a row for every one of them, including the ones with zero sites, so `declared` minus `observed` is empty by construction and a zero is a DECLARED ZERO rather than an absent key. Before this rule the construct map was built by `add()`, which creates a key only on a hit: the first whole-population artifact carried 42 construct keys and NONE of the four decisive counters, and a ruling read from it would have cited a number the document did not contain.
